script_text: Hello {customer_name}, this is {agent_name} from {company_name}. How are you today?
Hi {customer_name}, {agent_name} here with {company_name}. I’m reaching out to help you explore simple ways to protect your loved ones.
Good {time_of_day}, {customer_name}! Do you have a minute to talk about easy, affordable life protection?
I’ll keep this brief—about 2 minutes. If it’s useful, we can continue; if not, I’ll send a summary. Sound fair?
Before we start, is now a good time or should I schedule a quick call later today?
Thanks! I help people find the right coverage in minutes—no pressure, just options.
If you prefer, I can send a summary after our quick chat so you can review at your pace.
We’re regulated by {regulator} and keep everything transparent—fees, terms, and claims.
notes: Use early trust signal if prospect is skeptical

script_text: I see you’re based around {city}. How’s your week going?
Many people I speak with are planning for family and finances—does that sound like you?
I’ll tailor this to you—mind if I ask a couple of quick questions?
I help clients choose plans in under 5 minutes by focusing on what matters most to them.
If you have kids or financial goals, I can show options that fit right away.
Would you prefer I keep this very high-level or get into practical numbers?
To make this useful: may I confirm your age range—under 25, 25–40, 41–55, or 56+?
Do you currently have any life insurance coverage in place?
Which best describes your priority right now—protection, savings, retirement income, or health/accident?
Do you prefer monthly payments, or would annual payments with a discount be better?
Do you have a comfortable monthly budget in mind (e.g., {currency}500–{currency}2,000)?
Any major health conditions we should consider when recommending options?
If protection is the goal: roughly how much coverage feels right—{currency}0.5M, {currency}1M, {currency}2M+?
Do you have dependents (partner, kids, parents) who rely on your income?
Would you like optional riders like critical illness or accidental death?
Are you looking for a plan that builds savings/cash value, or strictly protection?
What prompted you to consider insurance now—new family member, mortgage, work, or peace of mind?
If something happened, which outcome matters most: replace income, pay debts, fund children’s education, or cover medical?
Would a policy focused on legacy (whole life) or flexible term protection fit better?
Do you prefer guaranteed values at maturity (endowment) or lower premiums with higher protection (term)?
Thinking ahead, do you expect your protection needs to grow (kids, bigger mortgage)?
Would you like a plan that can be adjusted later—coverage increases at life events?
Any specific concerns—accidents, cancer, hospital bills—you want covered?
For retirement, do you prefer a monthly income or a one-time payout plan?
Do you want your premiums or benefits to keep pace with inflation?
Is there someone else involved in the decision (spouse, partner) we should include?
Let’s pick a comfortable monthly range—would {currency}500–{currency}1,000 be okay, or {currency}1,000–{currency}2,000?
If we can start with a smaller premium and increase later, would that help?
Annual payments can save ~5–8%. Would you consider annual to reduce total cost?
We can show two options: lowest premium vs balanced protection. Which would you like to see first?
If budget is tight, we can add riders later. Would starting with core protection be better?
Do you prefer fixed premiums or the ability to index benefits over time?
If we lock rates today, it can save {currency}{potential_savings} over {years} years—would you like to see that comparison?
Would autopay/reminders help you stay within budget without worrying about missed payments?
A common way to size coverage is income × years. What multiple feels right—5, 10, or 15 years?
Do you want accidental death benefits added for specific events (traffic, travel)?
Would critical illness coverage that pays a lump sum upon diagnosis be valuable for you?
Are hospital income benefits important—for daily cash while hospitalized?
Do you prefer level coverage or decreasing coverage (e.g., mortgage-linked)?
Would you like multiple beneficiaries with percentage splits?
Should we factor in education costs for children when setting coverage?
Do you want the ability to increase coverage at major life events without full underwriting?
Any ongoing treatments or major diagnoses we should consider?
Are you a smoker or non-smoker?
Height and weight range (approx.) to estimate rates?
Any family history of critical illnesses (e.g., cancer, heart)?
Do you travel frequently or work in higher-risk environments?
If higher coverage is desired, are you comfortable with a quick medical check?
Would you prefer a plan that avoids medical exams (simplified underwriting)?
Any medication or allergies we should note for compliance?
Term vs Whole: term is lower cost for pure protection; whole life adds savings/cash value.
Endowment: pay for a set term and receive guaranteed maturity benefits.
Critical illness rider pays a lump sum upon diagnosis of covered conditions.
Accident rider enhances payout for covered accidents like traffic events.
Hospital income rider pays daily cash during hospitalization—helps with incidental expenses.
Free-look period lets you cancel within {free_look_days} days and get a full refund.
Grace period for missed payments is typically {grace_days} days; reinstatement is simple.
We are regulated by {regulator} and audited regularly; claims follow strict standards.
Approval time is often within {approval_hours} hours for standard cases.
You can manage your policy online via our app/portal—updates, downloads, and support.
I understand budget matters. Let’s start with a comfortable monthly and tailor coverage around it.
Totally understandable—I'll send a summary and schedule a quick follow-up tomorrow. What time works?
It’s smart to decide together—shall I share details for both of you and set a joint call?
We’re transparent—here’s the fee table and policy wording before any commitment.
Many healthy clients lock lower premiums early; it’s about preparing while rates are favorable.
Starting small is fine—core protection now, add riders later when budget allows.
Sorry to hear that—what happened before? I’ll make sure we avoid those pitfalls.
If timing isn’t great, I can send a 1-minute summary and set a 10-minute slot later.
Happy to compare neutrally against your criteria—price, coverage, waiting periods. Shall we do that?
We’re regulated by {regulator} and maintain strong solvency ratios. I can share independent ratings.
Understood. May I send a 30-second summary in case timing changes later?
If you’d like, we can lock today’s quote and you can decide after reviewing the details.
Based on your budget {currency}{budget_month}, here are two options: lowest premium vs balanced protection.
At {currency}{desired_coverage} coverage, monthly premium is ~{currency}{estimated_premium}.
If we add a critical illness rider, total premium becomes ~{currency}{premium_with_ci}.
Annual payment reduces cost by {discount_percent}%.
Decreasing term for mortgage keeps premiums efficient while tracking loan balance.
Whole life builds cash value—here’s the projection over 10 years.
Indexation keeps benefits aligned with inflation—opt in at {indexation_rate}% per year?
Bundle family coverage to save ~{discount_percent}% overall.
Starter plan today with option to upgrade later—keeps monthly within {currency}{budget_month}.
Here’s a side-by-side comparison vs your criteria: price, coverage, riders, waiting periods.
Shall we secure your coverage now? The application takes about {apply_minutes} minutes.
Would you prefer to complete this over the phone or via a secure link?
If we begin now, your coverage can start by {coverage_start} pending approval.
I’ll walk you through the disclosures and submit together—step by step.
We can lock today’s quote so you’re protected from rate changes while you review.
Would a starter plan make it easier to begin? We can upgrade later.
Do you want to add accident or critical illness riders now or keep it simple for today?
Great—let’s confirm your details and proceed with the quick application.
If you’d rather review first, I’ll send a tailored summary and set a quick follow-up.
Any final questions before we proceed?
I’ll send a concise summary with your options and a link to apply when ready.
What’s a good time tomorrow for a 10-minute call?
Would you like me to include details for your spouse/partner?
I’ll share the fee table and policy wording so everything’s crystal clear.
If you prefer chat/app, I can send the secure application link there.
I’ve set a reminder and locked your quote; you’ll receive a confirmation message.
Would you like educational guides (term vs whole, riders) sent to your email?
If timing changes, just reply ‘READY’ and we’ll proceed.
Before we proceed, I’ll read a brief disclosure about data use and product suitability.
This conversation may be recorded for quality and compliance—okay to continue?
I’ll verify your identity details and confirm accuracy for the application.
We’ll capture your health information strictly for underwriting and not share without consent.
I’ll summarize the key exclusions and waiting periods relevant to your chosen plan.
